strings.name: Sadiq Khan
strings.role: Mayor of London and Labour member of the House of Lords
strings.summary: Sadiq Khan is a British Labour politician and former human-rights solicitor. After local council, Commons and government service, he won London’s mayoralty in 2016 and was re-elected in 2021 and 2024. His administration introduced and expanded the Ultra Low Emission Zone, alongside transport, environmental and urban economic responsibilities. In 2026 he received a life peerage and entered the Lords while remaining mayor; these offices and their policy outcomes require distinct assessment.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 18 November 2026. Parliamentary records distinguish the peerage created on 20 August from the Lords introduction and oath on 15 September; City Hall confirms his mayoralty. Air-quality figures specify the modelled comparison and data period. Recent activity rests on the 6 November joint communiqué and 13 November meeting report.
strings.influence.rationale: As Mayor of London, advances transport, clean-air and urban inclusion policies and is an internationally recognised city leader.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and legal training
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Tooting, London, on 8 October 1970, he studied law at the University of North London and completed Law Society Finals at the College of Law’s Guildford centre in 1992–1993, the predecessor to the LPC. He subsequently worked as a human-rights solicitor.
strings.facts.f2.label: Public offices at different levels
strings.facts.f2.value: He was parliamentary under-secretary for Communities and Local Government from 5 October 2008 to 9 June 2009, then a transport minister of state, and held shadow justice roles in 2010–2015. The Mayor of London governs at Greater London level, distinct from the City of London’s Lord Mayor; his 2026 peerage does not change that distinction.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Interpreting air-quality estimates
strings.highlights.h1.text: The GLA’s March 2025 report estimated that London-wide roadside nitrogen dioxide concentrations in 2024 through September were 27% lower than a scenario without the ULEZ and its expansions. This is a modelled comparison, not a year-on-year fall or the isolated effect of the 2023 expansion. It does not mean every pollutant or health risk fell by that percentage.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Recent city cooperation and investment meetings
strings.highlights.h2.text: On 6 November 2026 he met Tokyo Governor Yuriko Koike in London to discuss AI, cybersecurity and climate cooperation. On 13 November he met business leaders in Istanbul to promote investment links. The communiqué and City Hall report confirm the meetings, not completed projects or funds already invested.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Introduced in the Lords as Lord Khan of Tooting
strings.timeline.t1.text: He was introduced, took the oath and undertook to follow the Code of Conduct. The life barony was created by letters patent dated the afternoon of 20 August. Creation, introduction and his continuing mayoralty are distinct; the peerage is not hereditary.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Wins a third mayoral term
strings.timeline.t2.text: He received 1,088,225 votes in the election held on 2 May, following victories in 2016 and 2021. This election used first-past-the-post rather than the previous supplementary-vote system. Polling day is distinct from the subsequent announcement of complete results.
strings.timeline.t3.title: ULEZ expands to all London boroughs
strings.timeline.t3.text: He extended the ULEZ across London, continuing charges for certain vehicles that fail emissions standards. The aim is to reduce polluting vehicles and exposure; air-quality improvement, drivers’ costs and accompanying support are separate evaluation questions.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Central London ULEZ begins operation
strings.timeline.t4.text: His administration introduced the Ultra Low Emission Zone in central London ahead of the originally planned start. It regulates vehicle emissions, is distinct from the congestion charge and is not a blanket traffic ban. The air-quality goals announced then required subsequent evaluation.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First wins the London mayoral election
strings.timeline.t5.text: He defeated Zac Goldsmith in the election held on 5 May, receiving 1,148,716 first preferences and 1,310,143 after transferred second preferences. Counts at different stages are not interchangeable. His Commons tenure for Tooting subsequently ended on 9 May.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes minister of state for transport
strings.timeline.t6.text: In Gordon Brown’s government he moved from Communities and Local Government to Transport, serving until 6 May 2010. Minister of state is distinct from the department’s secretary of state and from the mayoralty.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Elected MP for Tooting
strings.timeline.t7.text: He entered the Commons as a Labour candidate and retained the seat in 2010 and 2015. Parliamentary records show service until 9 May 2016, spanning three elections.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Enters Wandsworth Council
strings.timeline.t8.text: He was elected a councillor in the London Borough of Wandsworth and served until 2006, also working as a solicitor during this period. His council service preceded the mayoralty and partly overlapped his early Commons service.
